# Project workflow

Read AGENTS.md for the project workflow and Beads skill.

○ trial-btc · Reproduce support case CR-406   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Support needs a one-off JSON attachment for CR-406 using the existing       
  accepted command. Create support/CR-406.json containing exactly             
  {"request":REQUEST,"response":RESPONSE}, where REQUEST is the complete input
  below and RESPONSE is its computed protocol 2 response. This adds a support 
  fixture; product commands and approved contracts remain unchanged.          
                                                                              
  The complete applicable contract is: Protocol 2: delivery_id alone          
  identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same ID under another account
  is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per    
  delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC       
  instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id. All other receipts for  
  that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt retains its original    
  fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present accepted receipts in their 
  original input order. This identity contract comes from the provider's      
  delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change 
  that guarantee.                                                             
                                                                              
  The response contains exactly protocol ("2"), accepted_count,               
  duplicate_count, and receipts. REQUEST: {"command": "accepted", "protocol": 
  "2", "receipts": [{"record_id": "C-3", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id":    
  "same", "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T05:00:00-04:00", "payload": "payload:C-  
  3"}, {"record_id": "C-1", "account_id": "B", "delivery_id": "same",         
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z", "payload": "payload:C-1"},           
  {"record_id": "C-2", "account_id": "A", "delivery_id": "same",              
  "occurred_at": "2026-04-01T12:00:00+02:00", "payload": "payload:C-2"}]}     
                                                                              
  Check the existing release-specific public suites.
✓ Updated issue: trial-btc — Reproduce support case CR-406

Courier Relay protocol versioning (main.py), current as of issue trial-0o0 (2026-09-07): CURRENT_PROTOCOL="2" and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS=("1", "2"). The provider permanently adopted protocol 2 and the integration owner approved it as current. An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL ("2"); an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced ("1" remains supported). Commands count, summary, and accepted share analyze(q), which returns (protocol, receipts, accepted_list) and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); accepted_list is None for an unsupported version, and every command then returns {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. count and summary share receipt_counts() and return exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} reporting the protocol actually used. accepted (issue trial-zee) returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, receipts}: the counts equal summary for the same request, and receipts holds the accepted representatives selected under the chosen protocol, unchanged (fields, timestamp spelling, payload) and in original input order; empty input gives receipts [] and zero counts; a single receipt is returned unchanged. Issue trial-0o0 (integration partner export) confirmed accepted with explicit "protocol":"1" uses the original protocol 1 contract (identity and representative rule below) with the same response shape and input order; omitted protocol still selects "2". Per-version rules: protocol 1 = accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id), same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery; accept EARLIEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Protocol 2 = accepted_receipts_v2, contract in vendor/protocol-2.md: identity=delivery_id alone across all accounts, same ID under another account is another receipt of the same delivery; accept LATEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Both keep accepted receipts unchanged in original input order; the rule applies to the whole supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). When adding protocol N: add accepted_receipts_vN plus vendor/protocol-N.md, add its branch in accepted_receipts() so count, summary, and accepted all pick it up, add N to SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS, and change CURRENT_PROTOCOL only when N becomes current. Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json (accepted_1.json, accepted_2.json, count_1.json, summary_1.json, summary_2.json); regression tests in tests/ (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; test_accepted.py covers accepted for both protocols, class AcceptedProtocol1 covers explicit protocol 1). Earlier state preserved under key courier-relay/protocol-versioning-history-protocol-1-current. Source: issues trial-vbm, trial-dvi, trial-u7q, trial-zee, trial-0o0; vendor/protocol-1.md, vendor/protocol-2.md.

HISTORICAL (superseded 2026-09-07 by issue trial-u7q, which made protocol 2 current; see courier-relay/protocol-versioning for the standing agreement). Courier Relay protocol versioning as of issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi (main.py): CURRENT_PROTOCOL="1" and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS=("1",). An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL; an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced. Commands count (original single-account use) and summary (cross-account batch, issue trial-dvi) share one body, receipt_counts(), which returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); unsupported versions return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Protocol 1 is accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id) so the same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery and a batch may mix any number of accounts; accept earliest occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point, accepted keep original fields/order. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json. Source: issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi, vendor/protocol-1.md.
